{
  "verdict": "fix",
  "issues": [
    "The proposal invents a custom JSON schema for the API contract instead of using a minimal OpenAPI specification, unnecessarily forfeiting standard ecosystem tooling, code generation, and documentation capabilities.",
    "The contract only defines success status codes (200, 201, 204) and completely omits error response structures (e.g., 400, 404, 409), leaving clients without a standardized way to handle and parse failures.",
    "The GET /tasks endpoint returns an unbounded list of all tasks, which is a critical scalability and performance risk even for a minimalist API.",
    "The PUT endpoint lacks concurrency control mechanisms (such as ETags or a version field), which risks lost updates when multiple clients modify the same task simultaneously.",
    "The custom schema uses informal pseudo-types (e.g., 'enum: pending...') instead of strict data typing and validation constraints (e.g., required fields, maximum string lengths)."
  ],
  "suggestions": [
    "Replace the custom JSON schema with a minimal OpenAPI 3.0 specification to retain standard tooling and documentation capabilities while keeping the design simple.",
    "Define a standard error response object and include common error status codes (400, 404, 500) in the endpoint definitions.",
    "Implement basic pagination (e.g., limit/offset or cursor-based) for the GET /tasks endpoint, or explicitly define a hard maximum limit for returned records.",
    "Add an ETag header or a version field to the Task resource and specify its use in the PUT endpoint to handle concurrent modifications safely.",
    "Formalize the data types in the schema using standard JSON Schema types and explicitly define which fields are required for creation versus updates."
  }
}
